title: Rearchitect routing control plane: remove global cache and migrate policy evaluation to shard-local evaluators
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current routing control plane relies on a global in-memory cache of routing decisions and a central policy evaluator. This has caused several operational problems: high lock contention under bursty traffic, stale decisions during canary rollouts, and difficulty isolating regional outages. We've observed tail latency spikes and sporadic wrong-fallback behavior when the global cache is transiently inconsistent.

Goal: Replace the global cache + monolithic evaluator with a shard-local evaluator and a small, append-only change-log stream for cross-shard config changes. The new design should: (1) eliminate the global lock hotpath, (2) preserve deterministic policy outcomes, (3) allow safe progressive rollout of policy changes, and (4) keep recovery fast after node restarts.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change routing heuristics or add new policy types. It also does not modify client-facing routing APIs or the external router protocol.

Design summary:
- Introduce a lightweight per-shard PolicyEvaluator that owns policy state for the shard and evaluates decisions locally.
- Replace the global in-memory decision cache with a per-shard LRU read-through cache scoped to recent request keys.
- Publish policy changes to a small, ordered ChangeLog topic (Kafka/SQS abstraction) that shards consume; apply changes using a versioned diff and a two-phase apply for canary rollout support.
- Add a compatibility layer that supports both the old global evaluator and the new local evaluator during a staged migration (feature flag + cluster-level rollout).

Trade-offs considered:
- Centralized evaluator simplified cross-shard consistency but created a throughput bottleneck; moving to local evaluators gains throughput at the cost of requiring a reliable change propagation mechanism. We picked an ordered ChangeLog to keep cross-shard eventual consistency predictable and simple.
- We intentionally keep the per-shard cache compact to limit memory overhead; this favors more deterministic eviction behavior rather than unbounded caches.

Migration plan (high level):
1) Add PolicyEvaluator and per-shard cache behind a feature flag (read-only mode): shard-local evaluator can compute decisions but writes still update the global cache.
2) Wire ChangeLog producer on policy writes; implement shard consumer to receive changes and compute diffs.
3) Enable read-write mode for a single small cluster (canary) and run shadow traffic comparison with global evaluator for 48h.
4) Gradually flip clusters to new mode over two weeks, monitor divergence and fallbacks.
5) Decommission global cache and remove compatibility shim after no regressions are observed for 7 days.

Rollout safety: two-phase apply for policy updates (staged commit + activation) to avoid partially-applied policy states. Add a circuit-breaker that causes a shard to fallback to last-known-good local snapshot if ChangeLog consumer falls behind a configured threshold.

QA and testing: unit tests for evaluator semantics, integration test that replays policy change sequences, chaos tests that kill and restart shards while asserting deterministic outcome, load test to validate lock-contention removal.
acceptance_criteria: Per-shard PolicyEvaluator exists and can be enabled via feature flag
Global lock contention metric (routing_global_lock_p95) reduced by >= 60% under synthetic burst test
No customer-facing regressions in routing during canary (shadow diff < 0.1% mismatches)
ChangeLog processing lag < 500ms for 99th percentile under normal load
Global cache removed and deprecation PR merged with no open incidents for 7 days
migration_steps: Create PolicyEvaluator class and small LRU cache implementation (ENG-74201-01)
Implement ChangeLog producer for policy writes and consumer library (ENG-74201-02)
Add feature flag gating and compatibility shim to route evaluation codepath (ENG-74201-03)
Run canary cluster in read-write mode and collect shadow diff metrics (ENG-74201-04)
Progressive cluster flips and global cache removal (ENG-74201-05)
comments: 2025-01-12 - Maya Chen: Spike completed. Prototype reduced lock contention in local dev cluster by ~70%. See PR 1287 for microbenchmarks.
2025-01-20 - Engineering review: Agreed on ChangeLog approach. Concerns about ordering guarantees noted; decided to use ordered topic with at-least-once semantics and idempotent apply logic.
2025-01-27 - Security review: No new data plane secrets required; KMS access not needed for this change. Marked as not requiring additional security review.
2025-01-30 - Perf: Load test under 2000 rps spike shows routing_decision_latency_p99 improved by 18ms. Need to re-run with heavier shard count to validate linear scaling.
